papers.title_en: Chess\_db: A framework for working with large chess game datasets
papers.evidence: 国际象棋数据集框架，支持AlphaZero风格的象棋AI研究
papers.tldr: 国际象棋领域，在计算机引擎超越人类后，人类对局数据的分析对棋手训练愈发关键。然而，处理海量PGN（便携式棋谱）文件并快速查询特定局面下各颜色胜率仍是挑战。本文提出Chess_db框架，基于逻辑编程和开源键值数据库，自动化构建包含大量对局的位置表数据库，支持近乎即时的多维度查询（如白方胜率、黑方胜率）。实验表明，基于LevelDB等键值存储可高效管理数百万对局数据，查询延迟极低，显著提升棋手备战效率；且该框架设计通用，可扩展至其他棋类游戏数据分析。
papers.abstract_en: Chess is a two player strategic game that is embedded in classical AI  culture as it was once the frontier for intelligent behaviour.  There was the silent assumption that the advent of computer engines that  play better than the best humans will extinguish interest in the game. However, the opposite has come to pass, with a growing following for the game. A lot of the computational resources are now centered around training of players, where the engine output is just one aspect. Access to  past games is also an essential part, both in knowing what games a specific player has played previously, and also which continuations at a certain position have led to victory more often for each of the two colour players. We present Chess_db a suite of logic programming tools that can effectively manipulate games both in memory and via creating back end databases.  In particular, we provide versatile code that creates databases from PGN (portable game notation) game files and explore the suitability of open source key-value databases for  storing position tables that provide near-instant access to  information pertaining to substantially large number of games.
